_about: Test questions for the Ask page. Answers and quotes were written by the team from the challenge resources and checked word for word against the downloaded source text. 'must_have': every group must match at least one of its terms in the final verified answer. 'expect': 'answer' or 'abstain'.

questions.q: What caused the fire on Mir in 1997?
questions.answer: A solid-fuel oxygen generator canister ignited.
questions.quote: the canister ignited, shooting a three-foot flame

questions.q: How did the resident crew members normally meet their oxygen needs during standard Mir operations?
questions.answer: Through the electrolytic splitting of water.
questions.quote: The units, also now used aboard the International Space Station, generated oxygen through the electrolytic splitting of water, primarily reclaimed from sources aboard the station.

questions.q: What was identified as the most likely culprit for causing the solid-fuel oxygen generator to burst into flames?
questions.answer: Latex working glove material inadvertently introduced into the canister.
questions.quote: They identified the most likely culprit as latex working glove material inadvertently introduced into the canister.

questions.q: How was the Mir fire described in the history of spaceflight?
questions.answer: The worst in-orbit fire incident in the history of spaceflight.
questions.quote: following the worst in-orbit fire incident in the history of spaceflight.

questions.q: How many crew members were aboard the Russian space station Mir during the February 1997 fire?
questions.answer: Six crew members.
questions.quote: the six crew members aboard the Russian space station Mir faced significant danger when a fire ignited in an oxygen generating system.

questions.q: What is the capital of France?
questions.answer: Outside the knowledge base.

questions.q: Who won the 2022 football World Cup?
questions.answer: Outside the knowledge base.

questions.q: How much did the new firefighter backpack air system weigh?
questions.answer: 20 pounds.
questions.quote: New backpack system weighs only 20 pounds for 30 minute air supply, 13 pounds less than conventional firefighting tanks.

questions.q: How long could the new firefighter air tank system provide an air supply?
questions.answer: 30 minutes.
questions.quote: New backpack system weighs only 20 pounds for 30 minute air supply, 13 pounds less than conventional firefighting tanks.

questions.q: What was the pressure of the new firefighter air tanks?
questions.answer: 4,500 psi, twice the pressure of the tanks of the time.
questions.quote: They are pressurized at 4,500 psi, (twice current tanks).

questions.q: What materials were used to make the new firefighter air tanks?
questions.answer: An aluminum liner wrapped by resin-impregnated glass fibers.
questions.quote: Made of aluminum liner wrapped by resin-impregnated glass fibers, eliminating corrosion as well as lightening the load.

questions.q: How did the redesigned face mask help firefighters?
questions.answer: It permits better vision.
questions.quote: Redesigned face mask permits better vision.

questions.q: Where was the Brunswick Incipient Fire Detector originally used?
questions.answer: In Space Shuttle orbiters.
questions.quote: the Brunswick Incipient Fire Detector, originally used in space shuttle orbiters

questions.q: What does the Brunswick fire detector sensor detect in the air?
questions.answer: Combustion particles.
questions.quote: Sensor operates by sampling air to determine the presence of combustion particles

questions.q: How does the Brunswick fire detector reduce false alarms?
questions.answer: It tells combustion particles apart from dust.
questions.quote: can discriminate between combustion particles and extraneous matters such as dust.

questions.q: In which large-area application can many Brunswick fire detector sensors be linked to a central unit?
questions.answer: Mines.
questions.quote: For large area applications such as mines, any number of sensors can be linked to a central processor/display unit

questions.q: What makes the Brunswick fire detector different from commercially available smoke detectors?
questions.answer: It signals a fire condition before flame and smoke appear.
questions.quote: it senses and signals the presence of a fire condition before appearance of flame and smoke.

questions.q: What was the cabin atmosphere during the Apollo 1 pre-launch test?
questions.answer: 100% oxygen.
questions.quote: The astronauts would be wearing spacesuits with the spacecraft’s hatches closed and the cabin pressurized with 100% oxygen.

questions.q: What caused the Apollo 13 oxygen tank insulation to deteriorate?
questions.answer: Heat from the tank heaters, left on for an extended period.
questions.quote: During the final test on the launch pad, the heaters were left on for an extended period and reached temperatures around 1000 degrees Fahrenheit, degrading the Teflon insulation.

questions.q: What hatch did NASA fit after the Apollo 1 fire?
questions.answer: A unified hatch that opens within three seconds.
questions.quote: NASA also replaced the three-piece hatch with a unified hatch that could be opened from the inside or outside within three seconds.

questions.q: ما السبب الرئيسي لسرعة انتشار الحريق في Apollo 1؟
questions.answer: The pure oxygen atmosphere.
questions.quote: Because of the pure oxygen atmosphere, the fire spread quickly, causing a rapid rise in temperature and pressure that led to the rupture of the Command Module pressure vessel.

questions.q: ما أهم التعديلات التي أجرتها ناسا على نظام تخزين الأكسجين بعد حادثة Apollo 13؟
questions.answer: A third tank in a different bay, upgraded thermostats, no stirring fans, wiring sheathed in stainless steel.
questions.quote: For Apollo 14 and future missions, engineers at NASA and North American Rockwell redesigned the oxygen tank system by adding a third tank in a different bay, upgrading thermostats, removing stirring fans and sheathing all electrical wiring in stainless steel.
